thread:
Alex T.: Hey team — customer 789A reporting inconsistent behavior inside a single conversation after yesterday's rollout. Same user prompt sometimes returns a helpful answer, other times a terse refusal. Examples attached.
Maria L.: Got the escalation. They say it flips mid-thread, e.g. message1 -> full answer, message2 (re-sent same prompt) -> 'I cannot help with that'.
Samir (CS): Repro steps from customer: 1) Start convo id=conv_9f3 2) send system prompt + user question 'Summarize this policy' 3) send same user question again 4) sometimes different outputs. They captured 6 tries, 3 good / 3 refusals.
support-bot: NOTE: rollout v2026-03-04-23:45 toggled routing policy alpha -> enable_variant_fanout = true
Alex T.: I asked for request_ids and headers; customer supplied one request_id=rid_0009. They also included response headers. Two examples: 
```
200 OK
x-redwood-variant: rwd-v2-fp16
x-redwood-routing: primary
x-request-id: rid_0009
```
and later
```
200 OK
x-redwood-variant: rwd-v1-int8
x-redwood-routing: fallback
x-request-id: rid_0014
```
Maria L.: That suggests the request was routed to different variants mid-convo — likely due to capacity fallback. If variants have different safety/classifier behavior that would explain the refusal vs answer.
Julie (SRE): I see autoscaler events around the same window in prod-north-1: 
```
[2026-03-05T00:12:30Z] pool d-42 scale-down triggered
[2026-03-05T00:12:31Z] variant rwd-v2-fp16 pod removed
[2026-03-05T00:12:33Z] routing fallback to rwd-v1-int8
```
Samir (CS): Customer notes it happened in a short span (within 30s) inside the same conversation. They expect pinning to a single variant for session affinity.
Alex T.: Can we confirm whether session affinity is guaranteed during fanout/fallback window? I thought we maintained per-conversation pinning by conversation id.
Julie (SRE): Currently our routing guarantees affinity for 'active' sessions, but when an instance is OOM/crashed we fall back to compatible variant which can change behavior. We don't currently migrate KV cache between variant backends, so probability of changing output increases.
Maria L.: Customer is asking for root cause and mitigation — they'd like a hotfix or guidance to avoid mid-conversation flips.
Samir (CS): Repro command I used locally (sanitized): 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"conversation_id":"conv_9f3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this policy"}]}'
```
Alex T.: Quick mitigation options: 1) advise customer to pass `model_version` to pin to a model variant 2) disable fanout in their org config 3) ask platform to roll back the alpha routing change.
Julie (SRE): I'll check logs to see if fallback frequency spiked after the rollout. If autoscaler unstable, we may throttle scale-down or hold pods longer. Also will check variant safety classifier parity (v2 vs v1) — if classifiers differ that's a regression vector.
sre-bot: Incident watch created: IW-2026-1426 routing-variant-flip spike (owner: Julie).
Samir (CS): Customer requested reproducible evidence for an internal bug: they want a sample of both responses with raw token outputs and the response headers. I asked them to upload to the secure ticket.
Maria L.: For immediate customer-facing response: acknowledged, explained fallback behavior, offered pinning and temporary rollback. Customer wants ETA for fix.
Alex T.: Julie — can we provide ETA for safe mitigation (patch to preserve affinity OR rollback)?
Julie (SRE): I'll triage now. If it's an autoscaler tuning change/rollback we can push a revert within 2-4 hours. If it's classifier parity work, that'll take longer. I'll update the ticket and ping here.
Samir (CS): I'll keep customer updated and request the raw artifacts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
